scope.selection: All verified X, LinkedIn, or Instagram canonical public-evidence rows with a non-null platformPostId.
scope.authorIdentityPolicy: Native post URL or the first author profile link in the native post header only; comment/profile links are excluded.
scope.rawVisibleTextUse: Strict native LinkedIn primary-body extraction only: require exact URL Source activity ID, the primary Report-this-post marker, and a distinct engagement/footer or More Relevant Posts end boundary; exclude header/profile/navigation, media, engagement, comments, and related-post chrome.

method.directNativeAuthor: Resolve only URL-native identity plus structured authorHandle/accountUrl; rawVisibleText is removed for this stage.
method.opaqueLinkedinPayloadAuthor: For direct-unavailable LinkedIn activity URLs, parse only the first /in/ or /company/ link after the native post heading and resolve it globally across all three rosters.
method.companySubject: Accept a company subject only on exact company domain, exact bounded or narrowly normalized company name plus expected cohort, exact bounded company name plus at least two true rare catalog descriptors, or exact bounded/narrowly normalized company name plus a full roster-founder name. Batch/roundup lists and tangential credentials fail closed.
method.founderSubject: Accept a founder subject only when the assigned founder's full name appears in the primary authored body, allowing only Unicode diacritic-equivalent normalization. A company-strong body without the assigned founder is reassigned to the company subject, never retained as founder evidence.
method.hardMismatch: Reject the current subject without reassigning when it lacks a strong anchor, legacy/title evidence points to a different roster company, and no complete native primary body supports deterministic reassignment. A complete strongly anchored body is reassigned instead.
method.failClosed: Unknown, non-roster, or ambiguous authors are never promoted to roster owners. Strong subject validity is recorded separately from physical authorship.
method.primaryNativeBody: For the 88 previously unresolved subjects, verify the exact activity ID and primary Report marker, then bound the authored body before the first safe engagement/footer or More Relevant Posts boundary. A visible LinkedIn `…more` marker is usable only when a later safe boundary proves the post envelope; missing end boundaries fail closed.
method.narrowNormalization: Company normalization is limited to bounded alphanumeric token equivalence and the explicit terminal legal suffix in the catalog (the audited Enjamb Labs→Enjamb case). Founder normalization is limited to Unicode NFKD combining-mark removal (the audited Peter→Péter case).
method.negativeChromeControl: A target present only after ## More Relevant Posts or in comments/profile/navigation chrome is not primary-body evidence.

reasonDefinitions.direct_matched: A direct native URL or structured author field maps to exactly one roster owner.
reasonDefinitions.payload_author_recovered_unique: An opaque LinkedIn URL lacks direct author identity, but the native post-header profile link maps to exactly one roster owner.
reasonDefinitions.payload_author_non_roster: The native post-header profile link is present but does not map to any roster owner.
reasonDefinitions.payload_author_unavailable: Neither direct fields nor a native post-header profile link expose an author identity.
reasonDefinitions.direct_url_author_non_roster: The direct LinkedIn /posts/<author> URL exposes an author slug that does not map to any roster owner.
reasonDefinitions.mapped_account_owner_exact_owner: The uniquely mapped native account exactly matches the current batch, entity type, and entity ID.
reasonDefinitions.mapped_account_owner_catalog_id_normaliz: The uniquely mapped account is the same company owner, but the canonical row uses a legacy A16Z company entity-ID alias.
reasonDefinitions.mapped_account_owner_reassignment: The uniquely mapped native account belongs to a different entity and requires deterministic reassignment.
reasonDefinitions.unresolved_native_author: No unique roster author owner can be established; the row remains in review even when its subject is independently strong.
reasonDefinitions.valid_strong_third_party_company_subject: The company is independently and strongly identified while the physical author is unknown or a third party.
reasonDefinitions.valid_founder_subject_exact_full_name: The current founder is independently identified by exact full-name token sequence.
reasonDefinitions.unresolved_subject: Available title/text/submittedUrl fields do not meet the strong subject threshold.
reasonDefinitions.reject_subject_mismatch: The current subject conflicts with another roster company in legacy/title evidence, but the native primary body is unavailable or incomplete, so the row is rejected without reassigning.
reasonDefinitions.primary_multi_attribution: A LinkedIn payload-author recovery would change the author entity while an independently valid current subject must be preserved separately.
reasonDefinitions.secondary_direct_author_edge: A direct-author reassignment also has an independently valid company subject, but it is outside the opaque-LinkedIn payload gate.
reasonDefinitions.secondary_legacy_catalog_alias_edge: A payload-author reassignment has an independently valid A16Z company subject, but the current row uses a legacy company entity-ID alias.
reasonDefinitions.valid_native_body_company_subject: A complete native primary body strongly establishes and retains the company subject.
reasonDefinitions.valid_native_body_founder_subject_exact_: A complete native primary body contains the assigned founder's exact or diacritic-equivalent full name.
reasonDefinitions.valid_native_body_company_subject_requir: A complete native primary body strongly establishes a company, but the current row is founder-attributed and does not establish that founder; reassign the subject to the company.
reasonDefinitions.primary_body_end_boundary_missing_fail_c: The exact activity and primary Report marker are present, but no safe post-body engagement/footer boundary is captured.
reasonDefinitions.multi_company_batch_list_only: The target is only one entry in a multi-company cohort list.
reasonDefinitions.multi_partner_marketplace_list_only: The target is only one entry in a multi-partner marketplace announcement.
reasonDefinitions.multi_item_weekly_roundup_only: The target is only one entry in a multi-item news roundup.
reasonDefinitions.founder_name_in_multi_person_supporter_l: The founder is only one name in a multi-person supporter list, not the post subject.
reasonDefinitions.other_roster_company_only_tangential_ang: A different roster company appears only as an angel/advisor credential and is not the post subject.
reasonDefinitions.exact_company_name_without_approved_seco: The body names the company but lacks cohort, domain, roster founder, or two true rare catalog descriptors.

acceptanceImpact.currentGateImpact: All 41 strong subject rows remain author-unresolved/non-roster at the native-author gate; 38 retain their company/founder subject and 3 require founder-to-company subject reassignment without fabricating authorship.
safeAdjustment: Keep the native-author owner resolver fail-closed; do not map a non-roster author to the subject company or founder.
Add a separate subject-attribution acceptance path for metric-bearing posts that meet the strict company/founder subject rules in this audit.
Persist author status (unknown or non-roster) independently from subject attribution so opaque LinkedIn activity URLs can retain a valid company/founder subject without fabricating authorship.
Preserve both subject and author identities on the 13 primary multi-attribution candidates instead of replacing the valid subject when the author is reassigned.
